title: Stability Quickscan: Top Failures & Action Tracker — 2026-07-10
content:
Objective: quick, low-friction snapshot of the most actionable regressions observed during the last 7 days for new model onboardings and promptset sweeps. This is not a deep forensic — it's a priority-focused brief for engineers and owners to pick up fixes and checks.

Summary (one line): failure rate ticked up from 2.5% -> 4.8% (week over baseline), concentrated in three promptsets and two failure vectors; suggested short-term mitigations listed below.

Key metrics (7d window vs baseline):
- overall failure/quality-fail rate: 4.8% (baseline 2.5%)
- median latency: 86ms (baseline 80ms)
- p95 latency: 410ms (baseline 380ms)
- p99 latency: 920ms (baseline 760ms) -> responsible for ~12% of aborted requests
- hallucination score (promptset-weighted): +1.9 sigma vs baseline for KB-style summarization prompts
- format-violation rate (json/schema): 18% of fails, up from 9%

Top failure buckets (by count):
1) Hallucination-high-certainty (34% of fails)
   - Concentrated on promptset: streetlight-10 (urban-data summarization) and kb-summarize-v2.
   - Characteristic: model fabricates entity-level facts (dates/IDs) with high confidence; triage examples attached below.
2) Truncation / context-overflow (22%)
   - Issues when long-context tokens hit default chunking boundary; KV-cache eviction observed in some dedicated runs leading to partial answers.
   - Affects multilang-chat promptset when users include long transcripts.
3) Format violations (18%)
   - Responses that fail JSON schema (missing keys, stray markdown) — downstream parsers abort.
4) Latency tail causing client-side retries/aborts (12%)
   - p99 spikes correlate with batching threshold boundary changes on dedicated capacity pools.
5) Other (12%) — minor (hallucinated URLs, link-rewrite issues, minor hallucinations).

Representative failure snippets (redacted):
- streetlight-10 prompt (urban data summarization):
  "Input: monthly inspection logs for 12 lampposts — summarize anomalies and assign probable cause."
  "Model output: 'Lamp ID 3 failed on 2024-09-17 due to capacitor burnout' -> fabricated date not present in input."

- kb-summarize-v2 prompt (internal doc summarization):
  "Expected: bullet list with sources field.
   Actual: omitted sources, invented source 'Operations Whitepaper - Q3'"

- multilang-chat (long transcript):
  "Response truncated mid-sentence despite system prompt to always finish; KV cache logs show eviction at token 8192 boundary during a 1.2MB session."

Initial triage notes (what we checked):
- Confirmed regression started 2026-07-02 in our onboarding signal (coincides with model variant m-3.2q rollout).
- Quick baseline A/B: m-3.1 (control) has 2.6% fail rate vs m-3.2q at 4.7% on same promptset sample (matched traffic).
- Checked prompts for prompting drift: no template changes in PR history for these promptsets since 2026-06-28.
- Serving change correlation: kernel selection change landed 2026-07-01 (INF-1293) which altered attention tiling for seq>2048; potential root cause for truncation/formatting differences.
- Observed increased scalar underflow events in telemetry for quantized runner on 80GB A100 nodes (edge case with specific token distributions).

Immediate mitigations (short-running, safe):
- Rollback: pin onboarding traffic back to m-3.1 for streetlight-10 and kb-summarize-v2 (action: Samir, due 2026-07-12, jira MLONBOARD-872).
- Prompt-level guardrails: add explicit 'do not invent facts; return "unknown" when not present' postamble to kb-summarize-v2 and streetlight-10 (action: Evelyn, due 2026-07-13).
- Increase KV cache retention window on dedicated pools for multilang-chat to avoid eviction at 8192 boundary (action: Diego, infra ticket INF-1322, due 2026-07-14).
- Add lightweight JSON schema pre-flight for the top-10 critical routes; reject/prompt-retry on schema failures with soft-fallback to text output (action: Anika, PR draft at github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2345, due 2026-07-15).

Owners & action tracker (quick):
- Samir Gupta: rollback pin + run 24h smoke on pinned variant -> MLONBOARD-872 -> due 2026-07-12.
- Evelyn Park: prompt edits + internal prompt spec tests -> due 2026-07-13.
- Diego Morales: infra config (KV retention/tuning) -> INF-1322 -> due 2026-07-14.
- Lena Fischer: extended schema casting + parser-resilience tests -> due 2026-07-15.
- Anika Sharma: compile brief, re-run deck for Eng-ops sync + update Grafana quicklinks -> due 2026-07-12.

Longer-term investigations (queued):
- Deep kernel/quantization interaction analysis with model team — possible precision-edge cases when attention tiling changed; assign to research (Samir + Lina) -> ETA end of sprint.
- Evaluate secondary fallback model (smaller non-quantized variant) for quality-critical routes during peak hours (product/ops discussion required).
- Expand promptset fuzzing harness to include >1M tokens long sessions to replicate KV eviction patterns.

Notes, unknowns, and open questions:
- We still need to confirm whether hallucination increase stems from the model checkpoint change or from kernel/tiling change altering tokenization behavior. Which is more plausible? need modelling input.
- Are downstream parsers now more strict (schema enforcement) after the parser library update (PR #210 merged 2026-06-30)? if so, that could amplify visible format failures.
- Telemetry: need a list of 10 representative request-ids for each bucket to hand to model team; Diego to attach logs to INF-1322.

Quick checklist for reviewers:
- [ ] Owners confirm rollback window and smoke-test results (Samir)
- [ ] Evelyn posts revised prompt text and unit tests
- [ ] Diego verifies KV retention change doesn't break multitenant quotas
- [ ] Lena publishes parser resilience test results to confluence link above
- [ ] Anika publishes updated Grafana link + notifies #ml-quality with TL;DR

Context links & references:
- Grafana quickview: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quality/onboarding-quickscan?var-range=7d (copy this into slack post)
- Recent infra PR (attention tiling): https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/2299 (linked to INF-1293)
- Telemetry extraction notebook (working): https://notebooks.redwood.ai/ml/onboard-quick-extract.ipynb

Bottom line: schedule immediate rollback for the two highest-impact promptsets and push prompt guardrails while infra and model teams validate the deeper kernel/quantization interactions. This quickscan is intentionally conservative: prefer short-term quality wins that cost little customer-visible change.

---
Notes-to-self (scratch): consider adding a weekly automated 'quickscan' alert that snapshots top 5 failure buckets and triggers an on-call ping when total_fail_rate > baseline * 1.6. Also, consider a small eval harness that runs the new model variant on a stable promptset corpus before any rollout to avoid signal noise.

End of brief.
